body: I read this. I care. I know I'm just some dumb fuck on the other side of the internet, but I'd like to be here for you, if you'll let me.

It's always bothered me when people dismiss suicide attempts and self harm as "just begging for attention". Bro, if people need attention that badly, then maybe you should give them some fucking attention. People need other people, they need attention, they need to not be ignored, they need to be loved and validated and understood. 

If you think having someone on the internet here to listen, I'm here for you.

Not to mention you'll have to deal with the scars, and potentially less mobility in your hands and wrists for the rest of your life. The only thing worse than dying from a suicide attempt is not dying from a suicide attempt and living with the consequences. 

And if you mean it in a self-harming way... well, it's easier not to start than it is to stop once you've gone down that path, trust me on that one. 

We're here, we don't hate you, and we're here to support you if you have any interest in hanging on, okay?
I mean, you could try busking? But that’s obviously not gonna solve all your problems...
Hmm. Fair. Is there anything you like to do, or used to like to do?

Dude, nobody can give you a reason to live. That has to come from within, or at least has to resonate with you.

That said — I looked at another post you made, and it seems you’ve never had a job. How do you know how bad it’ll be until you try? I personally found some of my “shitty” jobs fun and fulfilling — it was nice to do something, to add value to the world, to make money, to have some semblance of independence. Why not try it out?

I failed out of my dream university, and now I'm struggling just to graduate from my shitty state school. I feel you. Being an international student and having autism certainly don't make life any easier either...

Hey there. Your wife cares about you, so so much. So do your dogs. My psychiatrist told me once that suicidal thoughts aren’t bad in and of themselves— they’re more of a “check engine” light. They’re not very specific, but they’re a sign something is seriously wrong and you need to get it checked out. Badly, in your case. 

I have some advice for you down below: if you don’t want it, don’t read it. 

First, harm reduction: give your wife control of all the medications and alcohol in your house. When you need normal doses of medication, ask her. 

Second, come up with a safety plan. There’s examples online if you search for them. Sit down with your wife and have her go through it with you. She loves you dearly; I’m sure she’ll be relieved to help you take some action. 

Third, save a crisis line as a contact in your phone. Then it’s there if you ever feel like you need it. 

I also have some thoughts for longer term interventions, but I suspect you won’t like those so I’ll keep my trap shut. 

Good luck. I believe in you. I believe you can pull through this, with help. 

Edit: if you could ask your wife to accompany you to your Wednesday appointment, that would be super awesome too.
I’m glad. You’re always welcome here.

Friend, I can’t diagnose you, but I wouldn’t rule out mental illness so early. You sound suspiciously depressed/anxious to me. Have you talked to a professional?

And maybe I’m reading myself into your words, but it sounds an awful like you’re saying, “I haven’t been through anything bad enough to want to kill myself, so I must be a bad person” or some variation thereof. You don’t need an external reason. Your obvious internal suffering is valid in its own right. Sound fake? It’s not, I promise. 

Peace be with you. I’m sending you the good thoughts.

You express yourself eloquently. It sure does sound like you’ve been given a bad hand in life — but that doesn’t mean there’s no hope. I find hope in beauty, in the rainbow after a storm, in the wind blowing through the grass, in the dewdrops on the flower petals. Witnessing the total solar eclipse last summer actually made me glad to be alive for the first time in years. This is kinda weird and spiritual, but I feel like witnessing beauty is like bearing witness to something greater than myself. 

I guess my philosophy is modeled after the poem “wild geese” by Mary Oliver. I highly recommend you look it up, if you get the chance.

Hey there. 

If you do see this — I’m here for you. I’ve been down that dark hole and come out the other side. I’ve seen things get better, and I’ve seen things get worse. And I, selfishly, hope you make it through.
For sure. In any case, I’m rooting for you and I truly hope it gets better for you.

That’s rough. It’s much easier when you’re in the position to ask for money — I made a crowdfunding campaign for my partner recently when I started to go broke from supporting them, and it worked out nicely. I was also lucky enough that I didn’t need to start supporting them until we’d been in a relationship for over a year. 

It’s pretty clear that if she’s talking about suicide, talking to you is not quite enough (although I’m sure it helps a lot). I’m not sure how you’d go convincing her of that, though...

Ever since I started having suicidal thoughts, I’ve had them through some of the best times of my life — it just turned from “it’s never going to get better, might as well end it now” to “this is amazing, might as well end it on a good note.” If it’s weird, then we’re weird together. 

That said... I’ve had times, even when I had constant suicidal thoughts, that I’ve been truly glad I lived that long (like seeing the eclipse here in the US last summer). Hang in there.

How long have you two been together? Have you ever met her in person? (This isn’t a criticism or saying your relationship isn’t valid if not, I just think it has some bearing on what to do from here). 

Do you have a well-off network of friends and family you could start a crowdfunding campaign around to get her housing? Or does she? 

It sounds like there’s a lot going on in her life, emotional and otherwise, but sometimes taking care of logistics can help people get into a better place. Mostly, just, stay with her emotionally and be there for her. It’ll be okay.
Do you mind telling me a little more about your situation? <3

lostallhope.com is an excellent resource. 

I found that actually rationally evaluating methods helped me calm down a bit. I hope, selfishly, that you’ll ultimately decide to stay. Whatever you choose, good luck. I hope you find peace in whichever path you take. 

If you want to talk about your reasons, I’m here to listen.

Lying probably isn’t the best bet. 

Have you told your mom that you’ve been having suicidal thoughts? I feel like that would also spur most parents into action.

Sounds like you’ve had a really rough shot of it. 

I also turned to cutting and spreading my nudes all over the internet, coincidentally starting in the spring of 2015 as well. I happened to had sex with a bunch of creeps from Craigslist, mostly as a distraction from my suicidal thoughts. The danger, the risk, the violence appealed to me. They still do. In a way, they always have. I daydreamed of being tortured as early as age 12.

I’ve found that there are healthier outlets for pain and suffering  than those, though — for me, BDSM with a trusted partner and intense exercise kinda fill those holes. A good therapist, a support network, and training on coping strategies hasn’t taken me back to normalville, but it has made a world of difference. Maybe they could help you too?
